newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids notationally stable after holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids notationally stable after holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices were notationally flat Friday amid the lack of business after the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
Nearly all heavy oil traders stayed home with the New York Mercantile Exchange and most utilities closed today.
Spot resid prices were supported in recent sessions amid firm natural gas prices and growing anticipation that enduser demand for resid would pick up after Thanksgiving.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent sulfur grade was notationally assessed at $22.25-50 a barrel, unchanged from Wednesday's level.
NYH December paper notationally held at $22.15-$22.35, flat from Wednesday's level. NYH January one percent paper remained at $22.25-$22.50.
High sulphurs in NYH also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $20.50.
The U.S. Gulf market was inactive, with one percent still at $19.50 and three percent at $18.25-50. USG December three percent paper was notationally discussed at $18.30-45, flat from Wednesday.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas was stable at $4.30s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was notationally assessed the same as Wednesday at about $4.75-90/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.53/mmBtu equivalent.
A upstate New York utility may seek up to 100,000 barrels of 1.5 percent sulfur resid in a tender next week, market sources said.
